summary: A researcher trained a neural network on 240 popular Christmas carols to write its own, producing humorous nonsense. The incident was later downgraded to an issue because no harm occurred.
technical_summary: A small neural text-generation model trained on a corpus of carols produced incoherent, amusing lyrics, illustrating limits of early generative language models. The only available report is an index page about downgraded incidents.
notes: Only report is an AIID index page on downgraded incidents; coded from the AIID description. Downgraded to an issue as humorous.

summary: A social media user reported that an AI image generator advertised on Instagram appeared to emphasize sexualized content about girls. The post raised concerns about misuse of generative AI for explicit or illegal material.
technical_summary: A generative image app promoted through Meta advertising was alleged to be used for inappropriate content focused on girls. The single source is a social media post expressing concern; no specific harm or output is documented.

summary: Research found that common recommendation systems built on collaborative filtering over-promote already popular items, giving users with niche tastes noticeably worse recommendations.
technical_summary: Collaborative filtering recommenders learn from aggregate behavior, so popular items are recommended disproportionately. Studies across music, movie, book and anime datasets showed users with little interest in popular items received the lowest recommendation accuracy.

technology.quote: Collaborative filtering (CF) is one of the most traditional but also most powerful concepts for calculating personalized recommendations

failure_mode.quote: users with less inclination to popularity (LowPop) receive statistically significantly worse multimedia recommendations

affected_population.quote: users with less inclination to popularity (LowPop) receive statistically significantly worse multimedia recommendations

notes: Academic finding about a technique, not a specific harm event.

summary: A Starship delivery robot on a university campus drifted off its path into a planter, needed help from passers-by, then moved on and fell down a set of stairs, as recorded by a bystander.
technical_summary: An autonomous sidewalk delivery robot lost traction at a path edge, failed to recover while trying to clear an obstacle, and later, apparently under remote control, descended stairs. The sequence showed limits in terrain perception and recovery behavior.

technology.quote: A Starship robot operating in autonomous mode begins returning to the depot.

failure_mode.quote: The robot's right wheels drop off the lip of the path, but the robot continues forward.

lifecycle_stage.quote: A Starship robot operating in autonomous mode begins returning to the depot.

notes: The author describes the sequence as exceptional rather than typical performance.

summary: Russian state-aligned television aired a fabricated video that appeared to show a senior Ukrainian security official admitting involvement in a deadly Moscow concert hall attack. Analysts said it combined real interview footage with AI-generated audio.
technical_summary: A synthetic video composited from two recent interviews was given AI-generated voice audio to put false words in an official's mouth. It was broadcast on a state channel to support a narrative blaming Ukraine, despite a separate group claiming responsibility.
systems: Deepfake video and AI voice cloning tools

summary: An Australian telecom company's new AI incident-management bot sent far too many technicians into the field. The team could not switch it off, and the fix project reportedly wasted several million dollars.
technical_summary: A bot intercepted all network incidents and chose among remote fix, technician dispatch, or human escalation. It favored costly technician visits and mishandled cases only humans could interpret. Because it was deployed all-or-nothing, it could not be disabled without overwhelming reduced staff.

failure_mode.quote: The bot, however, maximized on that choice.
the automation team was unable to turn off the bot

harm_type.quote: wasted several million dollars in the process

lifecycle_stage.quote: rolled out an AI program for its incident management process

severity.quote: wasted several million dollars in the process

notes: Single Medium account; the company is unnamed. Dispatch logic treated as an optimization algorithm.

summary: A couple driving home from a ski trip followed Apple Maps onto an unpaved, snowy mountain road and got stuck. Highway officials say navigation apps increasingly send drivers onto unsafe shortcuts in winter.
technical_summary: A real-time navigation app rerouted drivers around congestion via a residential side road that became unpaved and snow-covered. Routing optimized for travel time lacked reliable road-condition information, a pattern officials reported across several navigation apps.

failure_mode.quote: the tendency of real-time navigation apps like Google Maps, Waze, and Apple Maps to send drivers onto potentially unsafe roads

lifecycle_stage.quote: the latter guided them toward an unconventional route out of town

notes: Routing treated as an optimization algorithm; the couple were not injured per the excerpt.

summary: A Tesla using Autopilot crashed into a parked police car in Laguna Beach, California. The driver had minor injuries and the officer was not in the vehicle, which was totaled.
technical_summary: A Tesla driver-assistance system in Autopilot mode failed to avoid a stationary police vehicle, a recurring failure to detect stationary objects. Tesla said drivers must remain in control, and it was unconfirmed at the time that Autopilot was engaged.

sector.quote: A Tesla sedan in Autopilot mode crashed into a parked Laguna Beach Police Department vehicle Tuesday morning

technology.quote: The driver suffered minor injuries and told police she was using the car's driver-assisting Autopilot mode.

failure_mode.quote: latest example of semi-autonomous vehicles struggling to detect stationary objects

harm_type.quote: The Tesla driver suffered minor injuries, but refused transportation to the hospital.

lifecycle_stage.quote: A Tesla sedan in Autopilot mode crashed into a parked Laguna Beach Police Department vehicle Tuesday morning

severity.quote: The Tesla driver suffered minor injuries, but refused transportation to the hospital.

notes: Autopilot engagement was not yet confirmed when reported.

summary: A Tesla Model 3 driver in Greece said Autopilot suddenly veered right at a highway fork and hit a barrier. He was unhurt, and Tesla said the driver must stay responsible for the car.
technical_summary: A Level 2 driver-assistance system reportedly misread an exit fork and steered sharply toward a divider at highway speed. The driver, who said he was glancing at a navigation app, corrected too late. Tesla could not retrieve vehicle data.

technology.quote: Vehicle was engaged on Autopilot at 120 km/h. Car suddenly veered right without warning and crashed into the centre median

failure_mode.quote: the system became confused by an exit slip-road, jerking away from the straight-ahead lane unexpectedly

severity.quote: no other vehicle was involved in the Friday night accident and no one was injured

notes: Malfunction is the driver's claim; Tesla could not retrieve data and the driver admits reduced attention.

summary: Advocacy groups warned that a US immigration vetting system called ATLAS uses secret criteria, poor-quality data and sensitive personal information to flag immigrants and naturalized citizens, potentially leading to denaturalization.
technical_summary: ATLAS screens immigration case files against federal databases to flag fraud or security concerns, drawing on biometric data, watchlists and, in some circumstances, race, ethnicity and national origin. Its criteria are undisclosed, flags go to human officers, and critics cite risk of arbitrary, discriminatory results.

technology.quote: ATLAS looks for indicators that someone is dangerous or dishonest

lifecycle_stage.quote: Powered by servers at tech giant Amazon, the system in 2019 alone conducted 16.5 million screenings

affected_population.quote: Department of Homeland Security to scan the records of millions of immigrants can automatically flag naturalized Americans

notes: Harms are alleged by advocacy groups; specific wrongful outcomes are not documented in the excerpts.

summary: A widely used health risk algorithm underestimated the needs of Black patients, so fewer of them were selected for extra care programs than equally sick white patients, researchers found.
technical_summary: The algorithm predicted future healthcare cost as a proxy for health need. Because Black patients incurred lower costs at the same level of illness, they received lower risk scores and were enrolled in extra-care programs less often, cutting their share by more than half.

sector.quote: A widely used algorithm that predicts which patients will benefit from extra medical care

technology.quote: A widely used algorithm that predicts which patients will benefit from extra medical care

failure_mode.quote: software guiding care for tens of millions of people systematically privileges white patients over black patients
the algorithm used a seemingly race-blind metric: how much patients would cost the health-care system in the future

harm_type.quote: This had the effect of excluding people from the extra care program on the basis of race

lifecycle_stage.quote: The hospital automatically enrolled patients above certain risk scores into the program

affected_population.quote: A widely used algorithm that predicts which patients will benefit from extra medical care
This had the effect of excluding people from the extra care program on the basis of race

severity.quote: reduced the proportion of black patients receiving extra help by more than half

notes: The Washington Post report says the algorithm was not intentionally racist; Optum is working on a fix.

summary: Former employees alleged that ByteDance copied videos and account details from Instagram, Snapchat and other platforms onto its Flipagram app without users' consent, partly to train its For You recommendation algorithm on US content.
technical_summary: An engineering team scraped short-form videos, usernames and profile data at scale and republished them as fake accounts. Two former employees said the data was used to train the recommendation model to reflect US users' preferences. ByteDance denied any current connection.

technology.quote: The scraped content was used to train ByteDance's powerful "For You" personalisation algorithm on the US-based content

failure_mode.quote: took videos, usernames, pictures and more from the social media platforms and uploaded them to the app without users' consent or knowledge

lifecycle_stage.quote: The scraped content was used to train ByteDance's powerful "For You" personalisation algorithm on the US-based content

notes: Allegations rest on anonymous former employees; ByteDance said Flipagram is unconnected to current products.
